chunks: He said: Al-Sharif Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Jawani reported to me from Abu Talib al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn al-Muzaffar al-Alawi al-Umari, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masood, [from his father], who reported from Nasr ibn Ahmad, who reported from Ali ibn Hafs. He said: Khalid al-Qatawani narrated to us from Yunus ibn Arqam, who reported from Abdul Hamid ibn Abi al-Khansa, from Ziyad ibn Yazid, from his father, from his grandfather Farwa al-Dhafari, who said: I heard Salman (may God have mercy on him) say: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

My ummah will divide into three groups: A group upon the truth from which falsehood cannot diminish anything; they love me and love my household. Their likeness is that of fine gold -- whenever it is put to fire and kindled, it only increases in quality. A group upon falsehood from which truth cannot diminish anything; they hate me and hate my household. Their likeness is that of iron -- whenever it is put to fire and kindled, it only increases in evil. And a group of rolling stones upon the creed of al-Samiri; they do not say 'Touch me not' but they say 'No fighting.' Their leader is Abdullah ibn Qays al-Ash'ari.

key_terms.تفترق أمتي: My ummah will divide -- a prophetic warning about the splitting of the Muslim community
key_terms.مدهدهة: Rolling/wavering -- like a stone that rolls between two sides without commitment
key_terms.ملة السامري: The creed of al-Samiri -- reference to Quran 20:97 about the golden calf maker who said 'Touch me not', symbolizing fence-sitters who avoid engagement

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad prophesy about the three divisions of his ummah?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), as narrated by Salman al-Farisi, foretold that his community would divide into three groups. The first are people of truth who love the Prophet and his household; like fine gold, trials only purify them further. The second are people of falsehood who hate the Prophet and his household; like iron, trials only corrupt them further. The third are fence-sitters following the path of al-Samiri from the Quran (20:97), who refuse to fight for the just cause, led by Abdullah ibn Qays al-Ash'ari (Abu Musa al-Ash'ari). This prophecy describes the political splits that occurred after the Prophet, with the third group referring to those who abandoned Imam Ali at Siffin.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 3. He said: Al-Sharif Abu Abdillah, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Jawani reported from Abu Talib al-Muzaffar ibn Ja’far ibn al-Muzaffar al-Alawi al-Umri, from Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Masood, (from his father), who reported from Nasr ibn Ahmad who reported from ‘Ali ibn Hafs, who reported from Khalid al-Qatwai, who reported from Yunus ibn Arqam, who reported from Abdul Hamid ibn Abu al-Khansa, who reported from Ziyad ibn Yazid, who reported from his father, from his grandfather Farwah al-Zifari who reported that: I heard Salman, may Allah bless him with mercy, say: The Prophet (Peace be upon him and his progeny), said:

"My Ummah will be divided into three groups: a group on the absolute Truth, from which falsehood can reduce nothing. They will love me and my Ahlul Bayt, and their likeness is that of pure gold, which when put to the (test of) burning fire, increases in brilliance. And a group upon the false path, where Truth will reduce nothing. They will hate me and my Ahlul Bayt, and their likeness is that of iron, which when put to fire, increases nothing but evil. And a group like the rolling stones, following the path of Samiri. They would not say: ’Touch me not’, they would say: ’No fighting (for the just cause).’ Their leader will be al-Ash’ari. (i.e. Abu Musa al-Ash’ari)."
